items.title: Why is the period following the Maurya empire called the 'Age of Reorganisation'?
items.explanation: The period after the Maurya empire is known as the Age of Reorganisation because existing regions were broken up into new, competing kingdoms. This fragmentation occurred shortly after the assassination of Emperor Ashoka around 185 BCE, leading to constant territorial wars and political struggles for control across the subcontinent.

items.title: What values or principles guided emperors of that period?
items.explanation: The era saw a revival of Vedic rituals and practices. A key guiding principle was the performance of the Ashvamedha yajña, where a king declared his supremacy by leaving a horse to wander freely; any territory crossed unchallenged became part of his empire.

items.title: How did foreign invaders assimilate into Indian society and contribute to cultural confluence?
items.explanation: Foreign invaders, particularly the Indo-Greeks, entered the subcontinent. They contributed to cultural confluence by introducing new artistic styles, architectural forms, and literary traditions that blended with existing Indian culture.
